rows.why: Items 1, 2, 3 and 5 each cover part of S1. Item 1 is closest because the row order is what makes S1 specific. Its run sorted rows by createdAt, then by id (c, a, b). Items 2, 3 and 5 also agree: the output starts with the BOM, the header is exact, and every line ends in CRLF, the last one included.

Item 6 asks how the creation time is formatted. S2 wants the UTC date as YYYY-MM-DD, but the run wrote the full ISO timestamp, '2009-02-13T23:31:30.123Z'. The runs also show the status written as lowercase 'open' rather than 'Open', though no item asks about that. Item 11, empty field for a missing title, agrees with that part of S2.
Item 4 asks what an empty list produces. The run returned the BOM and the header row followed by CRLF, which is what S3 expects.

Item 12 asks how fields with separators are escaped. The run quoted a title holding a comma, quotes and a newline, doubled the inner quotes, and left '@cmd' unquoted. Not checked: whether a title starting or ending with a space gets quoted. RFC 4180 does not require that by itself.
Item 12 also asks about formula injection. The pick says leading formula characters are not neutralised, and the run wrote '=SUM...' and '@cmd' with no leading single quote. S5 requires that quote.

Items 7 to 10 each cover one of S6's invalid cases: unknown status, bad numbers, filled greater than openings, and an invalid date. In every run, building threw an Error naming the requisition id, as S6 expects. Item 7, unknown status, is listed first in S6, so it is named here.
